clue.text: Fractions of number in choppers to put on uniform on board

indicators.note: being on board a ship means sitting within its two letters

parts.note: on board a ship means between the letters SS, the steamship abbreviation

indicators.note: in an across answer, one piece put on another follows it

parts.note: uniform means even, level and regular

indicators.note: in says the number letter goes inside the word for choppers

parts.note: choppers is slang for teeth

explanation.surface: Someone working out fractions of a figure while fixing teeth and dressing in uniform aboard a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to put on' sets the choppers-with-number piece after EVEN, and the whole goes between S and S ('on board').
explanation.definitionFit: Each of seventeen equal parts of a whole is a fraction of this kind.

clue.text: From southern town, originally, and yet northern writer

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word town

parts.note: and yet means nevertheless, all the same

explanation.surface: A writer said to come from a southern town and yet to be northern.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a Scottish novelist, author of Treasure Island.

clue.text: Lead — a radioactive element? Not lead, it's a metallic element

parts.note: the lead or van is the front of an army or movement

indicators.note: not lead says to drop the front letter of the radioactive element

parts.note: radium is a radioactive chemical element

explanation.surface: A chemistry quiz: is lead radioactive? No, but the answer is a metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lead' first looks like the metal Pb; it means the van, the front. The second 'lead' means a first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Vanadium is a hard silvery transition metal, element 23.

clue.text: See 15
Listening devices from back of one shop near Barking

indicators.note: back of picks the final letter of the word one
barking means mad, so the following letters go crazy into a new order

explanation.surface: Buying headphones from a shop next to Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: Barking is a district of east London, but here it is the anagram signal for SHOP NEAR, giving ARPHONES after the E.
explanation.definitionFit: Headphones worn in or over the ears are devices for listening.

clue.text: One fat fly heads off, as ordered

indicators.note: heads off means each of the three words loses its first letter

explanation.surface: A single plump fly loses its head.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done tidily, in an ordered way, is done in a trim, orderly manner.

clue.text: Dangerous, so locked away at last

parts.note: locks of hair are what make a head locked in this whimsical sense

indicators.note: at last picks the final letter of the word away

explanation.surface: Something risky was secured and finally put away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'locked' looks like secured with a key; read 'so locked' as having locks, i.e. HAIR on top of the Y.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, a scary, risky situation is described as hairy.

clue.text: Grouped together with a retired joiner

indicators.note: a bed with a joiner in it holds the conjunction inside

parts.note: someone who has retired for the night has gone to bed
AND is a conjunction, a word that joins

explanation.surface: People gathered together alongside a carpenter who has stopped working.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joiner' suggests a carpenter, and 'retired' someone who has stopped work; they are AND and BED.
explanation.definitionFit: People banded together have formed a band or group.

clue.text: Drink for one that's picked up medal

parts.note: for one introduces an example, abbreviated eg

indicators.note: in a down answer, picked up means read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: a gong is British slang for a medal or decoration

explanation.surface: A drink, for example, for someone who has just collected a medal.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive drink of beaten eggs, milk, sugar and often spirits.

clue.text: Female's seduced by an ex-taoiseach

indicators.note: seduced by puts the female inside the two letters of an, taken in

parts.note: her refers to a female; 's is is, linking

explanation.surface: A woman is seduced by a former Irish prime minister.
explanation.definitionFit: Bertie Ahern was Taoiseach, Irish prime minister, from 1997 to 2008.

clue.text: Doctor grimaces, describing onset of nausea as being all too loudly evident

indicators.note: describing means drawing round, so the rearranged letters go around the other piece
to doctor is to tamper with, so these letters are altered into a new order
onset of picks the first letter of the word nausea

explanation.surface: A doctor pulls a face while describing the first signs of sickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' means drawing around: SCREAMIG, the anagram of GRIMACES, goes around N.
explanation.definitionFit: Something screaming is glaringly obvious, as in screaming headlines or a screaming error.

clue.text: Terrifying regular visitors to Dorset and Leeds

indicators.note: regular visitors call at every other letter of the place names, starting from the first

explanation.surface: Frightening people who keep turning up in Dorset and Leeds.
explanation.walkthrough: Dorset is an English county and Leeds a Yorkshire city; take their 1st, 3rd, 5th... letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreaded is feared, so terrifying in its prospect.

clue.text: Happy as a kingfisher?

definitions.meaning: relating to the mythical bird linked to the kingfisher, whose nesting calmed the sea

explanation.definitionFit: In Greek legend the kingfisher calmed winter seas, so the word came to mean idyllically calm and happy.

clue.text: Frees from tax in Norfolk town

indicators.note: in puts the tax inside the town's name

parts.note: Diss is a market town in Norfolk
to tax is to burden, as in a taxing load

explanation.surface: Exemption from a tax for those living in a Norfolk town.
explanation.walkthrough: Diss is a small market town in Norfolk, an English county; 'tax' is a noun meaning burden.
explanation.definitionFit: Relieving someone of a load is setting them free from it.

clue.text: Infuriated by golf shot, curse back-up supports

indicators.note: in a down answer, supporting means coming underneath the golf shot

parts.note: a drive is a long golf shot from the tee

indicators.note: in a down answer, back-up means the word reads from bottom to top

parts.note: damn is a curse word

explanation.surface: A golfer enraged by a poor shot, cursing while backing up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back-up' looks like a reserve; it turns DAMN into NMAD, and 'supports' sets it under DRIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To be made furious, enraged, by someone or something.

clue.text: Large dong one's confused with a "far out" snout

parts.note: L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

indicators.note: confused means the letters are mixed up into a new order

explanation.surface: A rude, comic mix-up of anatomy and noses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'confused' rearranges the letters of DONG ONES to give ONGNOSED after L.
explanation.definitionFit: Having a snout that sticks far out, a lengthy proboscis.

clue.text: Takes more off away kits?

parts.note: out means away, as in out of the office
strips are football kits, the team's uniform

explanation.surface: A footballer's away kit, and someone who takes more off.
explanation.walkthrough: In British football, strip is the word for a team kit. The definition plays on stripping more than others.
explanation.definitionFit: To exceed in undressing is a jokey literal reading; Chambers gives 'outdo in denuding oneself'.

clue.text: Model T Ford, on a return trip?

indicators.note: to model is to shape, so these letters are reshaped into a new order

explanation.surface: Taking a vintage Ford car out and back on a journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model T Ford' is a single car name; 'Model' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Going one way and then back again is a there-and-back journey.

clue.text: Leftward leaning flower

definitions.meaning: mildly left-wing or socialist in politics
a dianthus, a garden plant with fragrant blooms

explanation.definitionFit: A mild socialist is called pink, less than red; it is also a garden flower.

clue.text: A poet raving about Goat's Head soup

indicators.note: about puts the rearranged letters around the other piece
raving means mad, so these letters go wild into a new order
head picks the first letter of the word goat

explanation.surface: A poet ranting about Goat's Head Soup, a Rolling Stones album.
explanation.walkthrough: Goats Head Soup is a 1973 Rolling Stones album. POTAE, the anagram of A POET, goes 'about' G.
explanation.definitionFit: A thick soup, from the French word for soup.

clue.text: Arm that's hairy and small, short 3

parts.note: hairy is the answer to clue six down, so it stands for six
the answer to 3 down, shortened by its last letter, is a nose, slang hooter

explanation.surface: A hairy arm, and something small and short.
explanation.walkthrough: Two cross-references: 'hairy' is the answer to 6 down, so SIX; 3 down is NOSED, cut short to NOSE, which in British slang is a hooter.
explanation.definitionFit: A six-shooter is a revolver, and arms are weapons.

clue.text: Fish, catching record yields

indicators.note: catching means holding the record inside the fish

parts.note: rays are flat fish
an EP is an extended-play record

explanation.surface: A fishing trip where someone catches a record haul.
explanation.definitionFit: An investment that pays back, giving a return, is said to yield.

clue.text: Operating system in iMac involved a collection of bits

indicators.note: in puts the system's abbreviation inside the rearranged computer name
involved means tangled, so the letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A computer's operating system on an iMac handles lots of bits of data.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bits' looks like computer bits; it means small pieces. OS goes 'in' MAIC, the anagram of IMAC ('involved').
explanation.definitionFit: A picture made of many small tiles or pieces set together.

clue.text: 4,480-pound European, sounding like a siren

parts.note: a British ton is 2,240 pounds, so this weight is two tons

explanation.surface: A heavy European, oddly said to resemble a siren.
explanation.walkthrough: The imperial (long) ton is 2,240 pounds, so 4,480 pounds is two of them.
explanation.definitionFit: Police and ambulance sirens alternate between two pitches, a two-note wail.

clue.text: Ring relative who's missing lost cat

parts.note: a ring is shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: missing says a letter is taken out of the relative

parts.note: an uncle is a relative
L stands for lost, as in sports results tables

explanation.surface: Calling a relative about a cat that has gone missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ring' looks like a phone call; it is the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: Another name for the snow leopard, a big wild feline.

clue.text: Somewhat contrarily, spots no numbers around the clock

indicators.note: contrarily says the hidden letters are read backwards
Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone who notices nothing numerical at any hour.
explanation.walkthrough: The hidden letters POTSNON read backwards ('contrarily').
explanation.definitionFit: Continuing without a break, all day and all night.

clue.text: Like first of nurses taking city hospital round

indicators.note: round says the city and hospital are turned to read backwards

parts.note: LA is Los Angeles
a san is a sanatorium, a kind of hospital

explanation.surface: Nurses taking a ward round of a city hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the first letter of 'nurses' is N, a sound made through the nose.
explanation.definitionFit: N is a consonant voiced through the nose, so it is a nose-sound letter.

clue.text: Nice men in uniform, mostly Greek S&M nuts

indicators.note: nuts means crazy, so these letters are scrambled into a new order
mostly says the word Greek loses its last letter

parts.note: the ampersand is read as the word and, between S and M

explanation.surface: A risque picture of men in uniform, mostly Greek, into sadomasochism.
explanation.walkthrough: Nice is the French city, not the adjective. 'nuts' rearranges GREE with S AND M.
explanation.definitionFit: French police officers, as would be seen on duty in a city on the Riviera.

clue.text: Puck? Female, 6, non-starter!

indicators.note: non-starter says the first letter of that answer is dropped

parts.note: the answer to clue 6 down, meaning dangerous

explanation.surface: The setter, Puck, mock-describing himself as a female who failed to get going.
explanation.walkthrough: 6 is a cross-reference to 6 down. Puck is both the setter's pseudonym and the sprite in A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: Puck is the mischievous sprite in Shakespeare's A Midsummer Night's Dream, an example of the kind.

clue.text: Half-heartedly called police about son's minor indiscretions

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around into a new order
half-heartedly means losing half of the double letter at the heart of called

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Someone half-heartedly calling the police over their son's petty misdeeds.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Half-heartedly' drops one L of the middle pair in CALLED; 'about' rearranges CALED + POLICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Small sins or slight faults, from the Spanish for a little sin.
